lessons.title: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain how I found the area using the words base, height, area, and formula.

concept.heading: How do we find the area of a parallelogram?
concept.intro: A parallelogram is a four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides, like a leaning rectangle. Its area is how much flat space is inside it.
concept.keyIdea: Area of Parallelograms & Rhombuses. Formula: Area = Base × Height (A = b · h). 1. Identify the base (any side). 2. Identify the perpendicular height (height must be perpendicular to base, not slanted). 3. Multiply base times height; label with square units (e.g. cm², in²)

worked.title: Watch me
lines: I have a parallelogram with a base of 14 feet and a height of 9 feet.
I write the formula: A = base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = 14 × 9.
So the area is 126 square feet. I used the height of 9, not the slanted side.
linesEs: Tengo un paralelogramo con base de 14 pies y altura de 9 pies.
Escribo la fórmula: A = base × altura.
Entonces el área es 126 pies cuadrados. Usé la altura de 9, no el lado inclinado.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller parallelogram: base = 5 cm, height = 4 cm.
What is the formula? A = base × height.
What do we put in? A = 5 × 4.
What is 5 × 4? Yes, 20, so the area is 20 square centimeters.
linesEs: Ahora un paralelogramo más pequeño: base = 5 cm, altura = 4 cm.
¿Cuál es la fórmula? A = base × altura.
¿Cuánto es 5 × 4? Sí, 20, así que el área es 20 centímetros cuadrados.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.example: A = b × h; if b = 10 cm and h = 6 cm, A = 60 cm².

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.example: In a leaning parallelogram, use the dashed 90° height—not the slanted side—in A = b × h.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.example: Think of a leaning door — the top and bottom are parallel, and the two sides are parallel, like a slanted rectangle

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.example: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a parallelogram can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.example: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height at 90° to that side in A = b × h

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top.
vocabulary.example: A dashed vertical line from the top side straight down to the base, forming a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.example: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.example: A 3 cm × 4 cm rectangle covers 12 square centimeters — imagine 12 tiny 1×1 squares inside it

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.example: An L-shaped room = a 10×8 rectangle joined to a 4×5 rectangle; total area = 80 + 20 = 100 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.example: A = b × h means Area equals base times height; for a parallelogram with b = 6 and h = 4, A = 24

vocabulary.definition: A parallelogram with four sides of the same length.
vocabulary.example: All 4 sides equal, with two diagonals that cross at right angles.

vocabulary.definition: A segment that joins two corners that are not next to each other.
vocabulary.example: Corner to opposite corner.

lessons.title: Determine the Area of Triangles
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words base, height, area, and perpendicular.

concept.heading: How do we find the area of a triangle?
concept.intro: A triangle has three sides. The base is one side, and the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance from the base to the top corner.
concept.keyIdea: Area of Triangles. Formula: Area = ½ × Base × Height (A = ½ b · h). 1. Identify the base and the perpendicular height to that base. 2. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height. 3. Multiply base by height, then divide by 2

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My triangular garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I take half: ½ × 96 = 48. So the area is 48 square feet.
linesEs: Mi jardín triangular tiene una base de 12 pies y una altura de 8 pies.
Escribo la fórmula: A = ½ × base × altura.
Tomo la mitad: ½ × 96 = 48. Entonces el área es 48 pies cuadrados.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller triangle: base = 10 cm, height = 6 cm.
Now take half: what is ½ × 60? Yes, 30.
So the area is 30 square centimeters.
linesEs: Ahora un triángulo más pequeño: base = 10 cm, altura = 6 cm.
Ahora toma la mitad: ¿cuánto es ½ × 60? Sí, 30.
Entonces el área es 30 centímetros cuadrados.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.example: A = ½ × b × h; if b = 8 and h = 5, then A = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 square units

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a triangle can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.example: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height from the opposite vertex at 90° to that side in A = ½ × b × h

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.example: A dashed vertical line from the top point straight down to the base at a 90° angle — like dropping a plumb line

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.example: A triangle with b = 8 and h = 6 has area = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 sq units — exactly half the rectangle around it

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.example: The corner of a book or a door frame — the edges meet at exactly 90°, shown by a small square symbol

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.example: A house shape = a rectangle (the walls) + a triangle (the roof); total area = rectangle area + triangle area

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.example: A = ½ × b × h means Area equals one-half times base times height; for b = 12 and h = 8, A = 48

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.example: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

vocabulary.definition: Put the numbers you know into a formula.
vocabulary.example: A = ½bh → 30 = ½ × b × 5

support.prompt: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
feedback: You found 10 + 7; try multiplying instead.
Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
That label measures a distance along a line, but area describes the flat region a shape covers. Multiplying two lengths always produces square units.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.

support.prompt: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
feedback: Is the height half of 54?
Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.

support.prompt: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
feedback: Add base and height? The formula multiplies them.
You added 9 + 5; try multiplying.
22.5 is half of 45; is that the area formula?
hints: Spot the base (9 cm) and the height (5 cm). Which operation does the area formula use on them?
Use A = base × height. If your number looks like 9 + 5, or like half the product, rethink the operation.
Compute 9 × 5 and give the answer in square centimeters.

support.prompt: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The length of the slanted side
The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
support.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.
feedback: The slanted side is not perpendicular to the base.
Perimeter is around the shape; height is perpendicular distance.
The longest side is not always the height.
hints: Picture a leaning parallelogram. The height is not a side you can trace — it's a distance measured straight across.
Height must make a right angle (90°) with the base. Test each choice: is this perpendicular to the base?
Draw a base, then a straight up-and-down dashed line to the opposite side. That dashed line is what 'height' means here.

steps: Read the parallelogram: base = 7 ft, height = 4 ft
Write the formula: A = base × height
Substitute the values: A = 7 + 4
Calculate the area: A = 11 sq ft
support.explanation: Area uses multiplication, not addition. The formula is A = base × height, so A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Did the student add the base and height, or multiply them?
The area formula multiplies the base and height: A = 7 × 4 = 28 sq ft, not 7 + 4.

support.prompt: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
support.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
feedback: 16 comes from adding 10 + 6. Area means multiply the base and height, then take half.
The number is right, but cm measures length. Area needs square units (sq cm).
60 is base × height — the full rectangle. A triangle is half of that, so multiply by ½.
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.

support.prompt: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
feedback: 3 is 24 ÷ 8 — but that skips the ½. Double the area first: 2 × 24 = 48, then divide by the base.
12 is half of 24 — that divides by 2 instead of doubling. Try 2 × 24 = 48, then ÷ 8.
16 comes from 24 − 8. Use h = (2 × area) ÷ base instead of subtracting.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.

support.prompt: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
support.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.
feedback: Which two sides are parallel?
The height is perpendicular to them.
Identify bases and height correctly.
hints: Think about drawing a diagonal across a rectangle — what two shapes does it create?
Compare a triangle to a rectangle with the same base and height. How much of the rectangle does the triangle cover?
Sketch a rectangle, draw one diagonal, and shade one triangle. What fraction of the rectangle did you shade?

support.prompt: What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
feedback: TWO pairs would be a parallelogram.
Count the parallel pairs.
Exactly ONE pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid.
hints: Base 14 ft and height 6 ft — remember what makes a triangle's area different from a rectangle's.
Use A = ½ × b × h: compute the full product first, then halve it. Area needs square units.
Find 14 × 6, then take half of that product. Write the units as sq ft.

steps: Identify base and height: base = 9 ft, height = 4 ft
Write the formula: A = ½ × base × height
Multiply base × height: 9 × 4 = 36
Final answer: A = 36 sq ft
support.explanation: The student multiplied 9 × 4 = 36, but that is the area of the whole rectangle around the triangle. A triangle is only half of that rectangle, so the answer must still be cut in half: ½ × 36 = 18 sq ft.
hints: Look at the formula: A = ½ × base × height. Does the final answer include the ½?
9 × 4 = 36 is the rectangle's area, not the triangle's. What is ½ × 36?

support.prompt: Predict the area for these settings. Give the answer in square units. Round to four decimal places if needed.
support.explanation: 8 × 6 ÷ 2 = 24. A parallelogram with this base and height has area 48. The triangle has half as much area.
hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.
Use the relationship you explored in Investigate. Check with a second method.

support.prompt: A parallelogram has base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find its area in square centimeters.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

support.prompt: A triangle has the same base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area in square centimeters.
support.explanation: The triangle has half the matching parallelogram’s area: 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

steps: Read the parallelogram: base = 9 cm, slanted side = 10 cm, height = 6 cm
Write the formula: A = base × height
Substitute the values: A = 9 × 10
Calculate the area: A = 90 sq cm
core.explanation: The height is 6 cm, not the slanted side of 10 cm. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base × height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number was used for the height — the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90° angle) to the base. The 10 cm slanted side is not the height, so use 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.

steps: Identify base and height: base = 12 ft, height = 7 ft
Write the formula: A = ½ × base × height
Substitute values: A = ½ × 12 × 7
Calculate: A = (½ × 12) × (½ × 7) = 6 × 3.5 = 21 sq ft
core.explanation: There is only ONE ½ in the formula, not two. The student halved both the base and the height. Multiply base × height first, then take half just once: 12 × 7 = 84, then ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
hints: How many times does the ½ appear in A = ½ × base × height — once or twice?
Multiply 12 × 7 = 84 first, then take half a single time: ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.

steps: Identify base and height: b = 11 m, slant side = 8 m, h = 6 m
Write the formula: A = b × h
Substitute values: A = 11 × 8
Calculate: A = 88 sq m
stretch.explanation: The height is 6 m, not the slant side of 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m. Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which value should be used for h — the slant side or the height?
The height must be perpendicular to the base. The slant side is not the height.

stretch.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm. If you double the height, the area doubles too. Explain why this happens using the formula, and give a specific example with numbers.
stretch.frame: When the height doubles from ___ to ___, the area changes from ___ to ___ because in the formula A = b × h, the base stays at ___ and ___.
stretch.explanation: In A = b × h the base of 12 cm is a fixed factor, so the area is just 12 times whatever the height is. With h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; doubling to h = 10 gives A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactly double, because doubling one factor doubles the product.
hints: The base stays 12 cm the whole time — only the height changes. Your explanation should lean on A = b × h.
Pick an easy starting height (like 5 cm), find the area, then double the height to 10 cm and find the new area.
Compute 12 × 5, then 12 × 10. Describe what happened to the area when the height doubled, using the word 'multiply'.

steps: Identify base and height: b = 14 m, h = 9 m
Write the formula: A = ½ × b × h
Substitute values: A = ½ × 14 × 9
Calculate: A = ½ × 23 = 11.5 sq m
stretch.explanation: 14 × 9 = 126, then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m. The student added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying 14 × 9 = 126.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should happen between 14 and 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. The student added instead of multiplied.

stretch.prompt: A rectangle is 12 ft by 8 ft. A diagonal line cuts it into two triangles. What is the area of each triangle? Explain how the triangle area formula relates to the rectangle area formula.
stretch.frame: The rectangle's area is ___ because ___. Each triangle's area is ___ because a diagonal splits a rectangle into ___ equal triangles, so A = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___.
stretch.explanation: The rectangle's area is 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, and one diagonal cuts it into two identical triangles, so each triangle is 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. The formula says the same thing: each triangle keeps the rectangle's base of 12 and height of 8, and A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. The ½ in the triangle formula IS that diagonal cut.
hints: Start with the rectangle: its area comes from 12 × 8. The diagonal splits that area into two identical pieces.
Each triangle keeps the same base (12) and height (8) as the rectangle — so its area is half the rectangle's.
Compute 12 × 8, halve it for one triangle, then check with ½ × 12 × 8. Explain why both paths give the same number.
